cues.text: Three shots. Cover, frame one, host and dialog box hidden: our own workbench in daylight, a tape measure pulled out across it, the blade's numbers big, the gold end hook resting on the 160 mark; one focal object, the hero number "160" above the tape; plate "Missed call, 9 pm." / "One short text.", chip "MISSED-CALL TEXT". By 0.8 s cut in close on the tape's hook at 160 (the blade's ticks big, a missed-call phone lying on the bench beside it); Snow and the dialog box come in. On "short" cut to the third shot: the phone close up, MISSED CALL on its screen, a blank text bubble with a cursor and "0 / 160" under it.

The boss arena (r2; was street) under a night panel: ABOUT 1 IN 7 lands big on "about", seven phones pop in one a beat, the seventh rings red on "after" with "came after hours"; source tag "Source: ServiceTitan, June 2025" while it is said. On "Some shops" the panel lifts away: THE POLITE TEXT is the boss, our cream window over its menu types the usual paragraph. EXAMPLE tag.
The paragraph finishes: "Thanks for calling, we value your business."
NO NAME hits the boss and stamps on "name"; NO QUESTION hits and stamps on "question".
The last hit on "answer": the boss breaks into pixels and SKIP IT. stamps in; Snow waves.
The register set: WHO 29 rings on "Who", SORRY 26 on "Sorry", ASK 47 on "question", CHARS 102 prints as the total; the plate says "One question / to text back."

The text as an ITEM GET window (kit k.itemGet; the chime is its fanfare), EXAMPLE: "Hi, this is Sam the plumber. Sorry I missed your call. What do you need fixed, and when works for you?" Read aloud over the card: each part gets its slot colour bar as it is read; the counter under it counts up to 102 / 160, the tape strip fills to 102 under the 160 mark.
The scores set, title CHARS PER TEXT: row PLAIN 160 lands on "plain". Source tag up top while it is said: "Twilio docs: How long can a message be?".
Row EMOJI 70 lands in red; row CURLY 70 joins after "seventy" (the caption explains curly quotes).
Under the table: "Sam's text plus an emoji:" and "2 PIECES, 2 BILLS" stamps on "splits".
Back on the workbench, the tape out to 160, the clean text's 102 marked on the blade in teal. Card: "Tonight: put yours / in your auto-reply."
The rule lands in gold: "Short and plain. / Under 160." Snow waves. Then the end card with the send line: "Send this to whoever answers your phones."
